Based on the provided context, banks reported the impact of the FDIC special assessment as follows:

*   **Citigroup (Q4 2023):** Reported an FDIC special assessment of approximately $1.7 billion related to regional bank failures in March 2023, which impacted expenses in "all other."
*   **Wells Fargo (Q1 2024 and Q2 2024 Outlook):** Included $284 million ($0.06 per share) for the FDIC special assessment in its first-quarter results, noting this was an additional amount following a $1.9 billion charge in the prior quarter. For full-year 2024 guidance, Wells Fargo updated its non-interest expense outlook to approximately $54 billion (up from $52.6 billion), citing $336 million of expense for the FDIC special assessment in the first half of the year as a primary driver.
*   **PNC Financial Services (Q1 2024):** Reported a pre-tax, non-core, non-interest expense of $130 million ($103 million after tax) related to the increased FDIC special assessment. This amount was included in total non-interest expenses of $3.3 billion for the quarter.
*   **Bank of New York Mellon (Q4 2024 Outlook/Context):** While discussing Q4 2024 results, the transcript notes that reported expenses were down year-over-year primarily because the fourth quarter of 2023 included an FDIC special assessment.
